items.content_excerpt: $ONDS I don’t follow every ONDS update daily, but from what I see, this is a company still in its growth phase. It’s investing, expanding, building partnerships with companies like Palantir and Regna AI, and pursuing new contracts. Growth comes with costs. Sure, the stock is volatile, but this isn’t a company going from $50 to $2. It’s been swinging between $5–$7, with spikes to $12–$14. I own a small position and am considering adding at these prices. I’m not looking for overnight gains. I believe in the bigger picture. Some of the criticism seems excessive. There’s a big difference between a company that’s failing and one that’s investing to build its future. I’m open to criticism and corrections. If I’m getting something wrong, please point it out — just make it a reasoned argument. I’m always willing to learn.

items.content_excerpt: $CBRS 🚨 $CBRS COOLING SPIN EXPOSED: A Self-Inflicted 25 kW Flaw Cerebras PR hypes their "3D cooling" manifold, claiming they pioneered liquid cooling. Reality check: 1️⃣ Fake History: Cerebras didn't invent liquid cooling. Cray used it in 1985, IBM in 2010, & Oak Ridge ran liquid-cooled NVIDIA V100s in 2018—years before Cerebras. 2️⃣ Self-Inflicted Wound: Normal GPUs use standard heat spreaders. Cerebras built thousands of micro-nozzles only because a 215mm wafer breaks 2D heat transfer. It's a high-pressure plumbing liability. 3️⃣ CS-6 Pipe Dream Dead: Their diagram admits the wafer hits 85°C with a 45°C budget! DRAM leaks above 85°C. Stacking 3D DRAM on this 25 kW stove creates an insulating blanket that cooks memory. 4️⃣ Thermal Stress: CTE mismatch forces 24/7 "dummy workloads" to prevent cracking. $CBRS engineered a bespoke plumbing fix for a flawed monolithic architecture. https://x.com/milksandmatcha/status/2117386813023354958?a=lU-BAt4CPwv7bs5GvRA&s=46 $NVDA $SPY $AMD $IWM

items.content_excerpt: Microsoft $MSFT issued $25B of bonds on Oct 29 across ten tranches running from 2028 to 2066. Its total debt before the deal was $35.5B, so this added roughly 70% of its entire existing debt stack in one day. It was also its first US bond sale since 2017. Rated AAA, it priced ten-year money at 5.55%, about 64 basis points over the equivalent government bond. Microsoft generated $58B from operations last quarter against $39.4B of capital spending, the only one of the big five still clearly in surplus. items.title: Jim Cramer said falling oil prices and Treasury yields are driving a broad stock market rally, helping healthcare, financial, retail and tra
items.content_excerpt: Jim Cramer said falling oil prices and Treasury yields are driving a broad stock market rally, helping healthcare, financial, retail and travel stocks outperform as investors seek growth opportunities beyond technology. Brent crude plunged 7.63% to $104.77 per barrel on Monday, while the 10-year Treasury yield fell to its lowest level since September 10, improving the outlook for equities. Cramer highlighted Amazon, which gained 2% as lower interest rates helped investors reassess its recent earnings, and Waste Management (+1.8%), whose strong quarterly results had initially been overshadowed by rising yields. However, he warned that the simultaneous inflow of money into multiple sectors could make some gains difficult to sustain. Medical-device companies also benefited, with Medtronic rising 3%, GE HealthCare 4% and Intuitive Surgical 1%. Financials rallied as lower gasoline prices eased concerns about consumer finances, lifting Capital One 3%. $AMZN $GEHC $WM

items.title: Alphabet is seeking to raise €6 billion through its second euro-denominated bond offering of 2026, offering significantly higher yields than
items.content_excerpt: Alphabet is seeking to raise €6 billion through its second euro-denominated bond offering of 2026, offering significantly higher yields than in its May issuance as investor concerns over massive AI spending weigh on technology-sector credit markets. The seven-tranche offering spans maturities of two to 19 years and has attracted more than €17.1 billion in orders, with particularly strong demand for longer-term debt. Alphabet is offering an average new-issue premium of nearly 24 basis points, roughly three times the euro-market average this year. Pricing ranges from 40 basis points above mid-swaps for two-year notes to 185 basis points for 19-year bonds. Despite the higher borrowing costs, investors continue to view Alphabet's Aa2 credit rating and strong balance sheet as major advantages. Credit-market concerns have intensified as hyperscalers borrow heavily to finance AI infrastructure, while investors question whether the returns will justify the investment. $GOOGL

items.title: Marvell Technology’s proposed $115B all-stock acquisition of Lumentum has triggered significant backlash from shareholders of both companies
items.content_excerpt: Marvell Technology’s proposed $115B all-stock acquisition of Lumentum has triggered significant backlash from shareholders of both companies, with investors questioning the valuation, deal structure and potential benefits. The transaction values Lumentum at $1,132 per share, representing a 23.9% premium to its October 28 closing price. However, because the consideration is entirely in Marvell shares, the final value remains dependent on Marvell’s stock performance. The announcement sparked a sharp selloff on Monday, with Marvell shares plunging 12.72% and Lumentum declining 18.59%. Some Lumentum investors consider the offer unattractive despite the headline premium, while others are concerned that the all-stock structure exposes them to volatility in Marvell shares before the transaction closes. Marvell shareholders, meanwhile, are questioning the acquisition's enormous price tag, potential dilution and integration risks. $MRVL $LITE

items.title: Marvell Technology’s proposed $115B all-stock acquisition of Lumentum has triggered significant backlash from shareholders of both companies
items.content_excerpt: Marvell Technology’s proposed $115B all-stock acquisition of Lumentum has triggered significant backlash from shareholders of both companies, with investors questioning the valuation, deal structure and potential benefits. The transaction values Lumentum at $1,132 per share, representing a 23.9% premium to its October 28 closing price. However, because the consideration is entirely in Marvell shares, the final value remains dependent on Marvell’s stock performance. The announcement sparked a sharp selloff on Monday, with Marvell shares plunging 12.72% and Lumentum declining 18.59%. Some Lumentum investors consider the offer unattractive despite the headline premium, while others are concerned that the all-stock structure exposes them to volatility in Marvell shares before the transaction closes. Marvell shareholders, meanwhile, are questioning the acquisition's enormous price tag, potential dilution and integration risks. $MRVL $LITE

items.title: $SLS Stergiou wrote the following on June 3, 2021: "Additionally, most patients in CR2 status are rarely candidates for allogeneic stem
items.content_excerpt: $SLS Stergiou wrote the following on June 3, 2021: "Additionally, most patients in CR2 status are rarely candidates for allogeneic stem cell transplant, primarily due to their advanced age and low level of medical fitness, or for several other reasons, lack of compatible donors being a major factor. Typically, less than 10% of patients above 65 years of age, and less than 30% of younger patients, are able to undergo an allo transplant in CR2, especially if they had already received an allo transplant when they were in CR1, i.e., prior to their relapse." However, the criteria for the REGAL trial were even more restrictive: patients were enrolled precisely because they were not candidates for—or could not undergo—an allogeneic transplant. So, being generous, we are looking at a total of 5–6 patients.

items.content_excerpt: $SLS Ignore the comments about the 30% 3-year survival rate for patients in the BAT group. The BAT group has absolutely no chance of achieving such results because: These patients are very elderly. We don't know the exact median age, but it could be around 70 (plus or minus 2-3 years). They are not eligible for bone marrow transplantation. They are in CR2, and some of them already received venetoclax during CR1. This means that the leukemia is already partially resistant to it, and venetoclax won't be as effective. They are being treated with different methods; some are receiving Venaza and others are only receiving observation. Even if some patients increase the median OS in the BAT group, the remaining patients will decrease it. The maximum 3-year survival in the BAT group is approximately 20%, and the most likely 3-year survival is in the range of 5-15%. Everyone should do their own analysis and not be influenced by the opinions of others.

Marvell Technology’s proposed $115B all-stock acquisition of Lumentum has triggered significant backlash from shareholders of both companies, with investors questioning the valuation, deal structure and potential benefits. The transaction values Lumentum at $1,132 per share, representing a 23.9% premium to its October 28 closing price. However, because the consideration is entirely in Marvell shares, the final value remains dependent on Marvell’s stock performance. The announcement sparked a sharp selloff on Monday, with Marvell shares plunging 12.72% and Lumentum declining 18.59%. Some Lumentum investors consider the offer unattractive despite the headline premium, while others are concerned that the all-stock structure exposes them to volatility in Marvell shares before the transaction closes.
